html:
SMTO-PRL-0006 — SMTO rejected a group of steps before running them

GUID: f89b46fd-d12a-4435-8481-3da8d06008b8
Slug: parallel-validation
Domain: PRL · Subsystem: prl

What happened

  • SMTO tried to run several steps together, but one of them was set up wrong, so the group wasn't started. SMTO usually fixes this and tries again by itself.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Watch the conversation for a moment. SMTO normally reads the problem and sends a corrected group. The error tells SMTO exactly which step was set up wrong.
  2. If the same error repeats, send a message asking SMTO to run the steps one at a time instead of as a group. Running steps singly makes the faulty one easier to find and fix.
  3. If a step should run on a particular computer, make sure that Gateway is selected in the target menu (headed Execution target) when you send your request. A step aimed at a computer that isn't selected for the task is rejected.

What success looks like

  • The steps start and appear in the task's Activities section with their results.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep resending the same request unchanged; it will be rejected the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Activity batch construction or preflight rejected the batch (parallel_validation) because an item had invalid arguments, schema, target, identity or dependency bindings.

What this means

  • Batch construction/preflight catches argument, schema, target, identity or binding validation failures and returns a pre-execution rejection. Activity ownership, preflight and durable receipts determine admission and effect certainty. Rejected new work does not erase prior child effects; recovery and diagnostics never replay an unknown operation.

Why this can happen

  • Batch construction/preflight catches argument, schema, target, identity or binding validation failures and returns a pre-execution rejection.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the specific rejected field and child identity; this aggregate label does not identify a unique malformed argument.

How to fix it

  • Read the error and field in the rejected tool result, correct the named item against the current tool schema (arguments, target, id and depends_on bindings), and resubmit. Activities admitted earlier keep their identities and receipts.
  • Correct the reported batch field against the current advertised capability schema. Preserve existing activity identities and completed receipts.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The corrected declaration validates while preserving identities and receipts of already admitted work.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Activity ownership, preflight and durable receipts determine admission and effect certainty. Rejected new work does not erase prior child effects; recovery and diagnostics never replay an unknown operation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
